selected_topics.lesson_subject: Proxy-mode WebSocket UTM inspection for chatbot messages and file transfers
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: WebSocket protocol parser in proxy inspection exposes message frames and file transfers to DLP, antivirus, IPS, and file-filter engines; protocol options govern oversize and nested-compression scanning; proxy mode is mandatory.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Firewall policy -> proxy-mode WebSocket upgrade/parser -> UTM engines inspect message/file payload -> allow, block, and log.
selected_topics.failure_class: WebSocket payload inspection blind spot caused by flow mode, missing protocol options, or mismatched UTM feature set.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Proxy inspection mode; WebSocket protocol option; DLP/AV/file-filter profiles; controlled WebSocket payload test and UTM logs.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable WebSocket protocol options; use proxy mode; attach compatible UTM profiles; verify SSL inspection, oversize limits, and test payloads.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: WebSocket chatbot upload bypasses DLP because the proxy policy does not parse WebSocket frames.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Client -> TLS/WebSocket proxy parser -> DLP/AV/IPS/FileFilter engines -> application server; block/log branch.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from prior FortiGate DLP exact-data-matching: this lesson is the WebSocket protocol parsing/inspection path, not DLP pattern matching.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiAI task-scoped MCP agents and permission-bound management actions
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Task-scoped FortiAI agents expose FortiManager context and administrative functions through Model Context Protocol; agent selection controls task/tool scope while local administrator enablement, licensing, and RBAC constrain actions.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin selects task agent -> prompt/context interpreted -> MCP function callback requested -> FortiManager RBAC gate -> authorized operation -> callback result displayed.
selected_topics.failure_class: Agent or action unavailable because license, token budget, local-admin enablement, direct service reachability, or RBAC is missing.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: FortiAI license, `set fortiai enable`, selected agent, monthly token usage, callback result, admin profile and direct access to fai.fortinet.net.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Validate license/tokens; enable only approved local admins (maximum three); allow direct egress to fai.fortinet.net (proxy unsupported); scope RBAC; independently verify each resulting configuration change.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: FortiAI answers questions but cannot perform an authorized policy task; distinguish agent selection, license, local-admin enablement, and RBAC.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin -> FortiManager FortiAI pane -> task-scoped agent -> MCP callback -> RBAC gate -> FortiManager object/action -> callback result.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different product and workflow from prior FortiAnalyzer FortiAI alert triage; this is FortiManager management-action delegation and MCP/RBAC.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiAI data privacy: session-scoped masking and local function-callback execution
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAnalyzer masks IPs, MACs, and usernames before prompts pass through FortiAI proxy to hosted LLM; per-session cookie-derived mappings differ per session; callbacks return locally for unmasking and local analytics DB query; administrator-profile privacy masking is separate.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin prompt -> local sensitive-field masking -> FortiAI proxy/RAG -> hosted LLM callback -> local unmask and database query -> response with original identifiers.
selected_topics.failure_class: Privacy boundary misunderstood, or administrators assume all content including uploaded images is masked; confusion between prompt masking and administrator-profile privacy masking.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: FortiAI Masked Data view, original/masked text, function callback results, session context, and separate admin privacy-mask profile; does not prove image content is masked.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Inspect Masked Data and callback results; avoid sensitive topology-image uploads; use separate administrator privacy masking when required; maintain direct fai.fortinet.net access; validate local query results.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Original IP appears in returned answer; determine whether it was restored locally after a session-scoped masked prompt rather than sent to the LLM.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin -> local FortiAnalyzer mask map -> FortiAI proxy/RAG -> hosted LLM -> callback -> local unmask + analytics DB -> admin.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from 2026-11-07 FortiAI alert triage: this lesson is the privacy/masking and local execution trust boundary, not triage or evidence enrichment.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FortiSwitch link monitor multi-server probes and conditional static-route withdrawal
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch link monitor sends IPv4/IPv6 ARP or ping probes from a source interface to one or more servers; interval, timeout, failtime, recoverytime and update-static-route govern state; static-route changes require `set device`; supported only in default VRF.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Periodic probe -> per-server reachability evaluation -> failure/recovery counters -> server down/up state -> eligible static route withdrawn/restored.
selected_topics.failure_class: False or absent route failover due to wrong probe path, missing static-route device binding, wrong VRF, or aggressive thresholds.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: `get system link-monitor`; `diagnose sys link-monitor status all`; static route device binding; per-server status and route table before/after.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Set address mode, srcintf, server list, gateway/source IP, timers and retry thresholds; confirm default VRF; bind route to device; test each probe target.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Probe detects failed upstream server but static route remains installed because route lacks device binding.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch probe source -> multiple servers -> fail/recovery threshold state machine -> static-route device binding -> route install/withdraw.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from FortiGate BFD route withdrawal and Secure SD-WAN TWAMP SLA; this is FortiSwitch link-monitor probe state plus static-route binding.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: WPA3-SAE transition AKM selection and Wi-Fi 7 6-GHz H2E profile design
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: VAP security advertises WPA3-SAE or WPA3-SAE-Transition AKMs; `additional-akms akm24` permits SAE_EXT for capable clients while legacy clients use PSK_SHA256; 6-GHz WPA3 uses PMF, beacon protection, SAE H2E and optional AKM24-only for Wi-Fi 7 clients.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: VAP security and WTP radio profile provisioned -> AP advertises per-band RSN/AKM capabilities -> station selects mutually supported AKM -> SAE/H2E authentication and PMF association.
selected_topics.failure_class: Association failure or unintended compatibility loss caused by AKM mismatch, H2E/PMF requirements, or AKM24-only on non-Wi-Fi-7 clients.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: VAP `security`, `additional-akms`, `sae-h2e-only`, `akm24-only`, `pmf`, beacon-protection; radio-to-VAP mapping; client RSN/association logs.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Use WPA3-SAE with H2E/PMF on 6 GHz; use transition mode only where legacy compatibility is required; enable AKM24-only only for verified Wi-Fi 7 populations; map VAP to intended radio.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Wi-Fi 7 clients work on 6 GHz but legacy 5-GHz clients fail after AKM24-only is enabled; choose band-specific VAP/AKM design.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Controller -> FortiAP 5-GHz transition VAP and 6-GHz WPA3 VAP -> RSN/AKM negotiation -> SAE/H2E association.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from 2026-11-22 Wi-Fi 7 MLO and 2026-11-10 802.11k/v roaming; this is RSN AKM selection and SAE/H2E security negotiation.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Allowed-host quota accounting, per-user overrides, and adapter sibling semantics
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Global default maximum registered hosts per user can be overridden per user; scanned hosts or manually associated sibling adapters count as one host (up to five adapters), while unassociated adapters can count separately.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: User authenticates/registers endpoint -> host/adapter relationships resolved -> effective user quota selected -> count evaluated -> registration allowed or Over Registered Limit/Registration Failed.
selected_topics.failure_class: Quota appears exhausted because adapters are separate host records, user override supersedes global default, or administrator incremented limit.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: System > Settings > User/Host Management > Allowed Hosts; user properties Allowed Hosts and Registered Hosts; adapter sibling associations; registration result.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Review per-user override first; reconcile adapter siblings; confirm agent scan; set justified global/per-user quota; retest known adapter set.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Laptop with dock and Wi-Fi consumes multiple allowed-host slots; determine whether adapters are associated as siblings or counted independently.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: User -> registered host -> sibling adapters -> quota counter -> allow/deny; global default and per-user override.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from FortiNAC-F maximum concurrent sessions and endpoint adapter identity; this is FortiNAC per-user registration quota accounting.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Persistent Agent VLAN-switch acknowledgment when leaving remediation
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: 7.6.5 Persistent Agent acknowledgment appears only when switching out of remediation; cancel or timeout blocks VLAN switch; `User Canceled VLAN Switch` event-to-alarm mapping ensures next attempt prompts again.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint in remediation VLAN -> compliance clears -> agent prompts before transition -> accept allows switch; cancel/timeout blocks transition and emits alarm mapping -> next exit attempt prompts again.
selected_topics.failure_class: Endpoint moved without explicit acknowledgment or canceled/timed-out prompt is not repeated due to missing event-to-alarm mapping.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Persistent Agent Properties VLAN Switch Acknowledgment; `User Canceled VLAN Switch` event/alarm mapping; endpoint VLAN before/after; agent prompt and alarm timestamps.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable acknowledgment; verify event mapping; test accept/cancel/timeout; confirm remediation-exit event and switch-side VLAN transition; retest re-prompt.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: User cancels VLAN switch prompt once and is not prompted on next remediation exit; identify the new event-to-alarm mapping.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Remediation VLAN -> compliance transition -> acknowledgment decision -> VLAN switch allow/block -> event mapping -> re-prompt.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from prior Persistent Agent certificate, registry scan, and adapter identity lessons; this is a remediation-exit consent state transition.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: FSSO manual Active Directory server discovery for deterministic group lookups
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FSSO user-group membership discovery can query the global catalog automatically or be disabled in favor of explicit manual AD server list; automatic mode can restrict discovered DCs to configured Windows event log sources and remote LDAP servers.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FSSO group lookup -> discovery mode selects domain controllers -> LDAP/GC lookup contacts selected DC -> membership result maps to FSSO user group.
selected_topics.failure_class: Missing/inconsistent group membership because auto-discovery selects unreachable/unapproved DCs or manual list is incomplete.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Fortinet SSO > Settings > User Group Membership; Automatic/Manual mode; configured AD servers; event log sources and remote LDAP servers; FSSO and LDAP logs.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Use Manual mode in segmented domains and list reachable DCs; or keep Automatic and restrict discovered DCs to configured event-log/LDAP sources; validate DNS, LDAP ports, bind credentials and nested groups.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: FSSO logons arrive but group membership is missing because global-catalog discovery selects an unreachable DC; select manual discovery or restrict auto-discovered servers.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiAuthenticator FSSO -> global catalog automatic discovery or manual DC list -> LDAP group lookup -> user-group mapping.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from 2026-11-04 remote LDAP group filter inclusion; this controls DC discovery and lookup target selection, not group filter semantics.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: RADIUS Message-Authenticator request and response validation in FortiPAM 1.9
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiPAM 1.9 adds Message-Authenticator to RADIUS requests and `require-message-authenticator` on remote RADIUS server objects; default enabled requires validation of response attribute.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiPAM remote authentication -> Access-Request with Message-Authenticator -> RADIUS response -> response attribute validated with shared secret -> accept/reject.
selected_topics.failure_class: Legacy RADIUS server omits Message-Authenticator and FortiPAM rejects response after 1.9 default enforcement.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: `config user radius` server object and `require-message-authenticator`; packet capture attribute 80 in request/response; server logs.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Configure RADIUS server to return valid Message-Authenticator; verify shared secret and packet integrity; disable only as temporary compatibility exception after risk review.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: FortiPAM remote RADIUS logins fail after 1.9 because server omits Message-Authenticator; identify integrity attribute compatibility rather than user credentials.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM RADIUS client -> authenticated Access-Request -> remote RADIUS server -> response attribute validation -> accept/reject.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different product and transaction from FortiAuthenticator RADIUS proxy; this is FortiPAM remote-auth response integrity enforcement.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: Policy-based and CSV file-based Event Tagging in the event pipeline
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Collector enriches parsed events with custom attributes through ordered policy-based rules and CSV file-based lookups; policy tags execute first, file tags second; later matches can overwrite earlier values; each rule set has separate Apply action.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Collector parses event -> ordered policy tag rules -> ordered CSV lookups -> enriched event -> rules/reports/playbooks consume attributes.
selected_topics.failure_class: Incorrect/missing enrichment due rule order, later overwrite, malformed CSV mapping, organization scope, or saved-but-not-applied configuration.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Event Pipeline > Event Tagging rule order and enabled state; separate Apply indicators; Collector receives fresh events; event search shows tag.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Define stable CSV headers; scope organization; order rules intentionally; check overwrite precedence; Apply both rule sets separately; validate with new events.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Department tag is overwritten by later CSV mapping; identify policy-before-file execution order and Apply boundary.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Event source -> Collector parser -> policy tags -> CSV file lookup -> enriched event -> analytics/rules/reports.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from endpoint tagging and dynamic watchlists; this is Collector parse-time custom event-attribute enrichment.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: SPA server-to-client policy: initiating traffic from hub networks toward remote VPN users
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SPA server-to-client communication permits traffic initiated from SPA hubs or networks behind hubs toward remote users; current scope is VPN/agent users and requires Remote VPN plus edge-device user identification and additional FortiGate hub configuration.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Remote VPN user establishes agent tunnel/identity -> hub-side server initiates flow -> FortiSASE From hubs SPA policy matches scope/user/destination -> FortiGate hub route/firewall permits return path -> remote user receives session.
selected_topics.failure_class: Hub-initiated session fails because Remote VPN/user-identification prerequisites, From hubs policy, hub route, or firewall return path is missing.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Remote VPN and edge-device user identification enablement; From hubs SPA policy; hub routes/firewall; endpoint identity; packet capture at hub/PoP; client-to-server success does not prove server-to-client initiation.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Enable required Remote VPN and user-identification feature; create From hubs policy; add hub-side routes/policies; verify return path and user binding; test hub-initiated TCP.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: Remote users can reach internal servers but an internal monitoring server cannot initiate a session back; identify separate From hubs policy and Remote VPN prerequisites.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Internal server behind FortiGate SPA hub -> BGP/SPA overlay -> FortiSASE From hubs policy -> remote VPN agent endpoint -> return path.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from 2026-11-26 endpoint-to-endpoint and 2026-11-12 client-to-server; traffic initiation direction and identity prerequisites differ.

selected_topics.lesson_subject: SM3/SM4 IKE and ESP proposals for regulatory IPsec SD-WAN overlays
selected_topics.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS 8.0 adds ShangMi SM4 encryption and SM3 PRF/integrity for IKEv1/v2 site-to-site VPN proposals; Phase 1 IKE and Phase 2 ESP must match; SM4-SM3 uses SM4-CBC and HMAC-SM3.
selected_topics.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Peers exchange IKE proposals -> common SM4-SM3 transform selected -> Phase 1 IKE SA established -> Phase 2 ESP SA negotiated -> route-based overlay carries traffic; unsupported hardware/kernel prevents use or offload.
selected_topics.failure_class: Tunnel negotiation failure or unexpected performance because peer proposals mismatch, platform unsupported, or hardware acceleration assumed.
selected_topics.evidence_pattern: Phase1/Phase2 `proposal sm4-sm3`; `diagnose vpn ike gateway list name <tunnel>` shows sm4_128-sm3 and established SAs; platform/CPU support; SA state does not prove offload.
selected_topics.remediation_path: Expose IKE proposal options if needed; configure matching SM4-SM3 on both peers for Phase1 and Phase2; verify x86_64 supported platform and no hardware acceleration; test throughput after establishment.
selected_topics.question_fingerprint: An SD-WAN IPsec overlay fails after SM4-SM3 is selected on one peer only; identify matching Phase1/Phase2 proposals and platform support.
selected_topics.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: SD-WAN hub <-> IKE Phase1 SM4/HMAC-SM3 <-> Phase2 ESP SM4/HMAC-SM3 <-> overlay; platform/offload boundary.
selected_topics.semantic_review: Different from prior IPsec aggregation, ADVPN, FEC, and SD-WAN SLA topics; this is cryptographic proposal negotiation.
